events.label: AMD Advancing AI 2026 Day 1 (SF) + TSLA Q2 AH + GOOGL Q2 AH — week's triple binary; Intel Q2 AH follows July 23
events.note: AMD Advancing AI 2026 Day 1 at Moscone Center SF today — developer sessions and ecosystem announcements. Lisa Su keynote is Day 2 (July 23, 9:30am PT) and is the actual information event: MI450 accelerators, EPYC Venice, Helios next-gen roadmap, additional hyperscaler wins. TSLA Q2 AH tonight: 480K deliveries (record quarter) already known; gross margin consensus revised to ~19.5% with credits / ~18% without — raised bar vs. prior framing; options imply 7.6% swing. GOOGL Q2 AH tonight: Cloud backlog $462B; Q1 Cloud +63% YoY; consensus EPS $2.89 / revenue $116.84B; Anthropic 14% stake marked up — one bank projects GAAP EPS near $8 vs. $2.89 consensus; options imply 5.3% move. Context: WTI $87.56 / Brent $94.20 (crisis highs) on Rubio 'not serious' statement + 11th consecutive US strike on Iran; VIX 18.77; September hike probability ~69% (new formal breach). SPX needs second close above 7,480 tonight for the formal upgrade clock to complete. A double miss (GOOGL Cloud + TSLA margin) sends SPX through 7,480 with 5 of 7 regime breaches active — a configuration requiring immediate de-risking.

events.label: AMD AI Day 2: Lisa Su keynote 9:30am PT (MI450/Helios roadmap) + Intel Q2 AH (earnings)
events.note: Lisa Su's keynote is the actual product-information event: expected MI450 accelerators, EPYC Venice server CPUs, ROCm software updates, next-gen Helios rack-scale preview, and any additional hyperscaler wins beyond Microsoft Azure. AMD enters Day 2 having closed Tuesday at ~$503.57 after reversing a +4% premarket analyst-upgrade gap — the keynote needs NEW hyperscaler wins and explicit Kimi K3 inference-economics counter-arguments to move the stock structurally. Intel (INTC) Q2 AH July 23: consensus $14.4B revenue / $0.22 non-GAAP EPS / 39% gross margins; INTC surged ~8% Tuesday on three catalysts (up 163% YTD, down 17% from peak); options imply 15% move. Intel is the enterprise semiconductor demand bellwether — any guidance cut signals broader CapEx risk. IBM also reporting July 23 (enterprise tech bellwether; 94.4% historical beat rate).

events.label: Kimi K3 full open-weight model weights public release — second AI narrative wave; 2.8T parameter model
events.note: Moonshot AI scheduled to release the full Kimi K3 model weights (2.8 trillion parameters) publicly on July 27 — four days after AMD AI Day (July 22-23) and five days after GOOGL/TSLA earnings. AMD's Microsoft Azure Helios win (July 20) partially neutralizes the AI-capex-disruption premise heading into this event. If July 22 earnings confirm the AI demand thesis (GOOGL Cloud beat + TSLA margin beat), July 27 open-weight release will be less impactful. If July 22 disappointed on any major dimension, the open-weight release could re-activate the second DeepSeek trade and extend the semiconductor bear thesis beyond AMD AI Day. Do not add NVDA into July 27 — Kimi K3 open weights are a known risk catalyst regardless of July 22 outcomes.

events.label: FOMC meeting (Jul 28-29) — September hike probability ~69% (new formal breach above 60%); oil backdrop hawkish
events.note: As of July 22 morning: July hold probability ~76%; September hike probability ~69% — crossed the 60% formal trigger for the first time on the WTI $87.56 oil shock (was 48.7% in the July 21 night brief). WTI $87.56 / Brent $94.20 at crisis highs on Secretary Rubio's 'not serious' statement; the FOMC enters a hawkish oil-inflation backdrop with dual supply-shock (Hormuz + Houthi Saudi embargo) structurally active. The September language in the FOMC statement is the market-moving variable: dovish September language = immediate rate relief; hawkish September 50bps language = September hike probability jumps toward 80%+, extending the rate-shock regime through Q3. FOMC must decide whether to acknowledge the Hormuz/Houthi supply-shock in its inflation outlook — explicit acknowledgment is hawkish. Key: any FOMC statement that does not explicitly close the door on September is read as hawkish given where oil is.

events.label: META Q2 2026 earnings — AI cloud business quantification; MSFT Q2 + AMZN Q2 also; peak Q2 earnings week
events.note: META Q2 earnings July 29 is the first event where management must quantify the AI cloud business (Bloomberg July 1: Meta building AI cloud to sell excess compute). MSFT Azure must validate the AMD Helios deployment narrative with actual Azure AI revenue growth data. AMZN AWS is the third major hyperscaler read on AI demand thesis after GOOGL (July 22). META's ad-driven model is most insulated from Kimi K3 demand disruption. Peak Q2 earnings risk window.

events.label: July CPI release (est. Aug 13) — WTI $87.56 + Brent $94.20; dual supply-shock at crisis highs; most consequential macro print of 2026
events.note: July CPI is the first release to fully capture WTI at $87.56 and Brent at $94.20 — the crisis highs of the Iran-US conflict — amid the ongoing Hormuz blockade and Houthi maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia (~2.5M bbl/day at risk). CRITICAL UPDATE July 22: Secretary Rubio stated Iran is 'not serious' about peace talks and the US carried out its 11th consecutive evening of strikes, materially extending the ceasefire timeline. WTI/Brent at $87.56/$94.20 are the most severe oil levels of the crisis, with Brent approaching $95-100 where second-round inflation effects embed structurally. September hike probability has now reached ~69% (above the 60% formal trigger) on the oil shock. Bull scenario (July CPI <3.2% YoY with oil-shock not embedding in core): September hike probability collapses below 40%. Bear scenario (July CPI >3.5% YoY): September 50bps probability jumps toward 80%, BEARISH regime extends through Q4. The dual supply-shock (Hormuz + Houthi Saudi embargo) makes August CPI oil pass-through more structurally embedded than any prior 2026 single-event oil shock.

events.label: NVDA Q2 FY27 earnings (est.) — $91B revenue guide; AI capex cycle clearing event; addresses Moonshot AI + TSMC wafer hike
events.note: NVDA's Q2 FY27 earnings is the fundamental clearing event for the AI capex thesis. $91B revenue guidance represents sequential acceleration. AMD's Microsoft Azure Helios win (July 20) provides positive read-through for hyperscaler AI hardware demand. Risk factors: (1) TSMC 5-10% wafer price hike across ~74% of wafer revenue = 2-4pp gross margin headwind management must quantify; (2) Moonshot AI Kimi K3 (July 17) is a frontier-class open-weight model at 70% pricing discount that challenges hyperscaler GPU cluster inference demand — full open weights release July 27 will have occurred one month prior; (3) September hike probability at ~69% applies a meaningful discount-rate headwind to NVDA's ~37x forward multiple. NVDA held the $195 hard stop through the July 14-20 selloff — do not add until post-Q2 FY27 print with wafer hike impact clarified and Kimi K3 demand impact quantified.

events.label: SPCX first earnings as a public company (approx.) — Starlink ARR + Starship cadence
events.note: First earnings print since June 12 IPO. SPCX touched an intraday all-time low of $132.75 on July 15 (below $135 IPO price) — down 30%+ from June 16 ATH of $225.64. 27 of 31 analysts still carry Buy ratings; the sell-side downgrade cycle has barely begun. December 2026 lock-up expiry adds supply overhang. Re-entry gate: first earnings print (Starlink ARR growth, Starship launch cadence, cash burn) is the fundamental clearing event. Net losses are structural ($4.9B in 2025, $4.28B in Q1 2026). Better entry $115-120 for risk-tolerant 12-month investors.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut, early investors and insiders can sell, materially expanding the ~4% public float. Lock-up expiries are a known supply overhang for hot IPOs. The $20B bond offering (June 22) already changed the capital structure risk profile — the lock-up expiry adds equity supply overhang.

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window shifts to H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). SoftBank sold off -13% on the delay. Microsoft and NVIDIA hold strategic stakes. The delay removes a near-term AI sentiment catalyst and adds uncertainty to AI infrastructure spending trajectories.
